_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when an agent is making too many tool calls, when context is filling from verbose tool outputs, when the same…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "the agent made 17 read_file calls when 3 greps would have done — what should it have done?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the tool-call-strategy skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is tool-call-strategy the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes tool-call-strategy as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against context-engineering, refactor, debugging
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the tool-call-strategy workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore tool-call-strategy
Does not route to context-engineering, refactor, debugging when the tool-call-strategy scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
